name_zh: 莫卡尔巴里阿萨姆红茶
processing: Orthodox black tea: withered, rolled, fully oxidised and fired, with tippy lots sorted out as whole-leaf grades such as TGFOP1 and SFTGFOP1.
harvest_season: The second flush is the picking this garden is best known for; as usual in Assam, it falls in early summer.
appearance_dry: Dark twisted leaf with plenty of golden tips, larger and more even in the higher grades.
appearance_wet: Soft, coppery-brown whole leaf and tips.
taste_profile: Strongly malty and full-bodied, with fruit and honey notes described in second-flush lots.

brewing.notes: Brew it Western-style. Three minutes keeps it round; longer brings more grip and suits milk.

vintage_note: Sold by year, flush and grade, usually with an invoice or lot number on specialist lists. Second flush of the latest season is the normal purchase; like other orthodox Assams it is best within about two years. Tip-heavy auction lots are small and priced far above ordinary grades.
description:
Mokalbari is an orthodox Assam garden in Dibrugarh district, on the south bank of the Brahmaputra. Sellers list it among the classic names for a malty single-estate second flush with a lot of golden tip.

The method is standard orthodox work: the leaf is rolled rather than cut, oxidised fully, then fired and graded. Keeping the leaf whole is what preserves the tips and gives the higher grades a rounder cup than a plain breakfast blend.

Expect big malt first, then the fruit and honey that tasters often note in the second flush. Water near the boil and about three minutes works well. Oversteeping is the common mistake, since Assam turns harsh quickly, though a stronger brew takes milk nicely.

Buy by season and grade rather than by the garden name alone. Letters such as TGFOP1 describe the leaf and tip, not a promise of flavour, and lots vary from one invoice to the next, so a shop that names the year and flush is telling you something useful.
history:
The garden is usually dated to 1876 in trade descriptions, which also give it about 2,004 acres. A manager of Mokalbari Tea Estate, then described as being in Lakhimpur District, appears in the 1943 Birthday Honours, so the garden was well established by then.

In 2024 a small batch of its orthodox golden tips sold at auction in Kolkata for Rs 30,000 per kg, reported as a record. The estate's director put it down to a short spell of favourable weather during the peak of the second flush.
